segments.teaches: first guess: a period when GDP keeps rising is a period of economic growth; but is that the right definition?

cream band over the climbing stretch

blue question with an arrow: is this the right way to define growth?

segments.notes: sets up a definition only to break it in the next segment
segments.idea: it is tempting to call any long rise in GDP 'growth'
segments.shown_as: an empty GDP-vs-year chart; dots drop in one by one and join into a line that dips and then climbs; a cream band rises over the climbing stretch, titled period of economic growth, and a blue question with an arrow challenges it

segments.teaches: GDP rose 10 lakh -> 50 lakh but population rose 1,000 -> 10,000, so per-capita income fell 1,000 -> 500: rising GDP alone is not growth

elements.what: value tags 10 lakh and 50 lakh on two points
red drop-lines from the two points to population labels 1,000 and 10,000
yellow per-capita income band with 1,000 and 500 under the drop-lines
grey box over the rising stretch
green 'positive GDP growth' and red 'per capita income decreased'
growth title turns pink and gets a red cross

segments.notes: counter-example built on the same chart; the cross lands on the title, not on a sentence
segments.idea: if people grow faster than GDP, each person gets less, so GDP growth alone is not economic growth
segments.shown_as: two points on the rising GDP line get value tags (10 lakh, 50 lakh); red drop-lines fall from them to population labels (1,000 then 10,000); a yellow per-capita band fills in 1,000 under the first and 500 under the second; a grey box covers the stretch with a green 'GDP up' tag and a red 'per-capita down' tag; finally the 'economic growth' title turns pink and gets a red cross
segments.example: GDP 10 lakh -> 50 lakh, population 1,000 -> 10,000, per-capita income 1,000 -> 500

segments.teaches: economic growth is a sustained increase in per-capita income

PERIOD OF ECONOMIC GROWTH returns beside the band

segments.notes: same chart grammar as the failed definition, only the y-axis changes: a clean 'fix the definition' move
segments.idea: growth means income per person keeps rising over a long time

segments.teaches: even with rising per-capita income, poverty can rise and literacy fall (made-up figures)

segments.teaches: growth may not reach 138 crore people because government money goes to e.g. defence rather than health and education

segments.teaches: a better quality of life is economic development; until the 1960s growth and development were used as the same thing, yet some countries had high growth and low quality of life

elements.what: quality of life = economic development, under the crowd
dotted line with a 1960 tick
arrow back to a note: both terms were used interchangeably
presenter at a chart board
countries A, B, C: growth high, quality of life low

segments.notes: the WHY and government branch clear; the crowd stays as the subject of 'quality of life'
segments.idea: development is about people's quality of life, and the world learned around the 1960s that growth does not guarantee it
segments.shown_as: the WHY and government branch clear away; under the crowd a blue equation appears (quality of life = economic development); a dotted timeline runs below with a 1960 tick: an arrow back points to a note that the two terms were used as one, an arrow forward points to a presenter at a chart beside a small table where countries A, B, C show high growth but low quality of life
segments.example: countries A, B, C: high growth, low quality of life

segments.teaches: trickle-down theory said growth automatically lifts quality of life; the evidence broke it, and in the 1970s a Pakistani economist set growth apart from development

TRICKLE DOWN THEORY with a line to its claim
curved arrow from the theory toward the high-growth/low-quality table, cut by a red cross
presenter icon turns green
real photo of the economist with a national flag, pulled out by a pointer
'economic growth ≠ economic development'
note on the 1970s distinction

segments.notes: real person photo (BIE will not use); the red cross on the arrow refutes the theory with the table's evidence
segments.idea: the belief that growth trickles down to everyone failed, so growth and development were separated
segments.shown_as: the camera moves in on the 1960 timeline; under the purple note a 'trickle-down theory' heading drops a line to its claim (growth lifts quality of life by itself); a curved arrow from it toward the high-growth/low-quality table is cut with a red cross; the presenter icon lights green and a pointer pulls out a photo of the economist with a 'growth ≠ development' tag and a short 1970s note

segments.teaches: growth is the lower step; development is the higher step growth should lead to
